title: Wittmann leads a BMW one-to-seven at Zandvoort
dek: Marco Wittmann won Saturday's Zandvoort race from second on the grid by 0.464 seconds as BMW filled the first seven places, while championship leader Jamie Green went off in the gravel.

chapters.title: BMW arrive without a win
text: Zandvoort was the fourth weekend of the 2015 DTM season, and it arrived with the pecking order well established. Audi had won four of the first six races and Mercedes-Benz the other two, while BMW had yet to win at all. Jamie Green led the championship on 81 points from Mattias Ekström on 70 and Pascal Wehrlein on 67, and Marco Wittmann, the reigning champion, was outside the leading six.

The dune circuit looked like the place where that could change. Audi and Mercedes-Benz were carrying performance weights after their results, which left the BMW M4 DTMs as the lightest cars in the field, and Zandvoort is hard on its tyres, so a lighter car had a clear advantage. Each of the three brands fielded eight cars, 24 in all, for a Saturday race of 40 minutes plus one lap.

The weekend also brought the DTM's new slow zones, a speed-limited stretch of track meant to clear stranded cars without a full safety car, which the series planned to use in a race for the first time. Conditions were dry, sunny and warm, around 20 degrees on race day, with a field that had watched BMW struggle through the first three weekends.

chapters.title: Farfus takes pole by eight thousandths
text: Qualifying turned into a BMW show. Augusto Farfus put his RBM M4 on pole with a 1:31.266 in the closing stages of the 20-minute session, after the track had been getting quicker all the way through. Marco Wittmann and António Félix da Costa both lapped in 1:31.274, missing Farfus by 0.008 seconds, and Wittmann took the front-row place beside him because he had set his time first.

Maxime Martin completed an all-BMW top four in 1:31.363, 0.097 seconds off the pole. Gary Paffett was fifth in 1:31.570, the best of the Mercedes by a wide margin: Wehrlein, in the other leading Mercedes, would start ten places behind him in 15th. Green was sixth in 1:31.627 and the best Audi, 0.361 seconds slower than Farfus, and only Miguel Molina, in tenth, joined him in the top ten from that brand.

Timo Glock, Tom Blomqvist and Bruno Spengler took seventh to ninth, so seven BMWs lined up in the top nine. Martin Tomczyk, 14th, was the only BMW driver outside the top ten. Ekström started 19th and Timo Scheider 21st, Paul di Resta was 22nd and Maximilian Götz was last of the 24 in 24th. Farfus said the balance had been good all weekend and that he was looking forward to racing his BMW colleagues around him.

chapters.title: Wittmann jumps the pole-sitter
text: Wittmann made the better start from second and went down the inside of Farfus before the first corner. Félix da Costa and Martin also got by as the pole-sitter fell to fourth, a drop Farfus later put down to a slipping clutch at the start. Wittmann said the grip on the line had been the key to the win.

The safety car came out almost at once. Paul di Resta ran into the back of Robert Wickens' Mercedes on the opening lap and slid into the tyre wall, which ended his race before he had completed a lap. The field ran behind the safety car for about five laps while the car was recovered. At the restart Wittmann led from Félix da Costa, Martin, Farfus, Paffett and Green, and the next ones out were Tomczyk, who stopped with a brake problem at the end of the neutralisation, then Edoardo Mortara after six laps and Molina after 13.

chapters.title: Green runs wide and a first for the DTM
text: Wittmann and Félix da Costa edged clear of Martin and settled into a two-car race for the lead, with Paffett and Farfus fighting over fourth behind them. On lap 15 Wickens, who had survived the first-lap contact, went out as well. Two laps later the order was shaken by the championship leader: Green, sixth and under pressure from Spengler, ran wide at Turn 9, went into the gravel and was stuck.

His stranded Audi triggered the first use of the slow zones in a DTM race. Instead of calling the safety car, race control limited the second sector to 80 kilometres per hour while the car was recovered, and the cars were able to keep running. Green was left without points for the weekend's first race, though his lead in the championship would survive it.

chapters.title: Wittmann holds off Félix da Costa
text: With roughly ten minutes left Félix da Costa began to attack, looking down the inside at Tarzan on several laps, but Wittmann covered each move and won by 0.464 seconds in 42:30.240. Wittmann said afterwards that the DRS on the car behind had made it impossible to break away, while Félix da Costa said he had not wanted to take a risk at the end. Martin finished third, 2.229 seconds behind, and Félix da Costa set the fastest lap, a 1:33.462 on lap nine.

Behind them Paffett pushed Farfus hard for fourth to the end, but a lunge in the closing minutes ended with light contact and the Mercedes running wide through the gravel at Schievlak, and he dropped to 11th. Farfus held fourth, ahead of Spengler, who had started ninth, and Glock, and Blomqvist took seventh with the first points of his DTM career. The seven BMWs finishing first to seventh was the first time a manufacturer had done so in the series. Mike Rockenfeller was the best of the rest in eighth for Audi, Nico Müller ninth and Wehrlein tenth, taking the last point.

The win was Wittmann's first of the season and BMW's first of 2015. In the championship Green still led on 81, 11 points clear of Ekström, who had finished 13th and stayed on 70. Wehrlein moved up to 68 and Wittmann climbed to sixth on 39.

facts.v: BMW took the first seven places, the first time a manufacturer had finished one to seven in a DTM race.
